localFindings.description: Any third party can make exitAndSeed permanently unexecutable for THIS escrow (and any redeploy of the same code) for ~1 wei + gas: transfer 1 wei of sUSDS or phUSD to the canonical pair and call pair.sync() (reserves become non-zero, so the skim branch is skipped and PairNotEmpty reverts), or mint a dust first-LP directly via pair.mint. Even a skim-less, one-sided reserve state cannot be seeded through Router02 (UniswapV2Library.quote reverts INSUFFICIENT_LIQUIDITY), and the escrow seeds only via Router02 with the exact-empty gate. The story classifies this as 'DoS only; abort returns funds' — correct for funds (abort is unaffected), but the escrow has no recovery mode: completing the cutover after poisoning requires abort + a DIFFERENT contract (direct transfer + pair.mint which tolerates one-sided reserves, or a seed-at-existing-ratio path). Redeploying UniPoolerCutoverEscrow will fail identically because the pair is the factory-canonical one fixed by UniPoolerV2 (PairNotCanonical). Front-running is possible whenever exitAndSeed is broadcast publicly, and the poisoning can also be done any time before.
localFindings.codeQuote:
if (r0 == 0 && r1 == 0 && (b0 != 0 || b1 != 0)) { ICutoverPairSkim(_pair).skim(_newPooler); ... }
if (r0 != 0 || r1 != 0 || b0 != 0 || b1 != 0) { revert UniPoolerCutoverEscrow__PairNotEmpty(r0, r1, b0, b1); }
localFindings.crossRef: phStaging run-39 L-01 (2-wei pair poisoning blocks story-103 core; recovery seed must be atomic); UniPoolerV2 L-24 (dust pre-seed, wont-fix). Escrow does not worsen funds-at-risk; it inherits the DoS and lacks a recovery branch.
localFindings.recommendation: Broadcast exitAndSeed via a private relay; have a pre-built fallback seeding contract (direct transfer + pair.mint, tolerating dust reserves within a bounded tolerance) ready, or add a bounded 'dust-tolerant' mode to the escrow. Not a funds-loss issue.

localFindings.description: Only four tokens can ever leave the escrow (_bpt, _sUSDS, _phUSD, _usds). Any other ERC20 sent to it is permanently locked (no rescue, no owner). The BPT address is SNAPSHOTTED from oldPooler.pool(), which is owner-mutable via BalancerPoolerV2.setPool, while BalancerPoolerV2.withdrawBPT transfers IERC20(_pool) — the CURRENT pool. If oldPooler.setPool is called between escrow deployment and withdrawBPT(escrow, amt) (or the owner hand-transfers a BPT of a different pool), the BPT that lands on the escrow is not _bpt: exitAndSeed reverts NoBPT and abort does not return it, so it is permanently stranded. Likewise any mis-sent token (e.g. USDC, a wrong BPT, an LP token) is unrecoverable. Story open question #5 accepts 'no rescue for tokens outside the four (INFO)'; the setPool interaction is the non-obvious part.
localFindings.recommendation: Operational: assert escrow.bpt() == oldPooler.pool() immediately before withdrawBPT in the cutover core (story-103), and never call setPool during the cutover window. Optionally allow abort() to return an arbitrary non-protected token to oldPooler (destination still fixed, so custody guarantee is preserved).

localFindings.description: Exit slippage protection is entirely the operator-supplied minAmountsOut, validated only as length==2 and each >0. A 1-wei floor is accepted. The array is passed straight to the V3 Router in Balancer pool-token order (sorted by address: sUSDS 0xa393.. before phUSD 0xf3B5.. on mainnet); the escrow neither validates order nor recomputes the proportional share of the combined BPT. A mis-ordered array either reverts (safe) or silently loosens one token's floor. The seed itself has NO price/ratio floor: Router02 mins == desired only enforce exact consumption on an empty pair, not a price. Story open question #1 — confirmed as described.
localFindings.codeQuote: if (minAmountsOut.length != 2) revert ...; for (uint256 i = 0; i < 2; i++) { if (minAmountsOut[i] == 0) revert ...ZeroMinAmountOut(i); }
localFindings.recommendation: Defer to econ/script audit: the phStaging2 core must compute floors over the COMBINED escrow BPT (incl. owner's 202.30) in Balancer token order with a tight tolerance.

storyOpenQuestions.codeBehaviour: Confirmed. Only length==2 and each>0 (L256-259). Floors forwarded verbatim to the V3 Router in Balancer token order; no proportional-share recomputation, no ratio/price check on the seed.

Confirmed. s/p = balanceOf(this) AFTER the exit (L268-270), so any pre-sent sUSDS/phUSD (and any BPT sent to the escrow, L252) joins the seed; minAmountsOut bounds only the exit leg, not stray balances. Because the seeded LP is 100% newPooler's (empty pair), a stray donation is a gift to protocol POL — a donor cannot profit from shifting the seed price (donate-then-arb nets the donor a loss in constant-product). The only party who can exploit a mispriced seed is an arbitrageur trading against a seed price that differs from the external phUSD price, which exists independently of donations (see Q6).

Confirmed DoS-only for funds: unsynced donation is skimmed to newPooler (L365-371); synced donation or a dust first-mint reverts PairNotEmpty (L372-374). abort() has no pair dependency. Escrow has no recovery path; a same-code redeploy fails identically.

Confirmed. _operator is immutable (L95, L213); every state-changing fn including abort is onlyOperator (L176-179). No owner/second key/timelocked fallback. Key loss strands all four balances permanently.
storyOpenQuestions.status: accepted design; Law-3 trusted; not a finding

storyOpenQuestions.codeBehaviour: Confirmed. Only _bpt/_sUSDS/_phUSD/_usds are ever transferred (L296-299, L415-418). Non-obvious extension: the BPT is a snapshot of owner-mutable oldPooler.pool(), and withdrawBPT pays the current pool.

Confirmed. Seed ratio = exit proceeds ratio (+ any stray balances); proportional exit returns the Balancer pool's composition ratio, which is NOT a price check against $1 or any oracle. Router02 mins==desired (L400) only pin exact consumption on an empty pair. Post-seed arbitrage toward the external phUSD price is an economic question (econ-scanner).

otherObservations: Recovery vs proportional is operator-chosen (enum), never clock-derived — matches story.
